solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brief dissembling is rare in a drama

parts.note: brief, as in short and abrupt in manner, means curt

indicators.note: dissembling means disguising, so the letters of 'is rare in a' are put in a disguised order

explanation.surface: A brief bit of pretence is uncommon in a play, someone remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drama' at the end is the definition; 'dissembling' is the anagram signal working on the four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain-raiser is a short play staged before the main piece, so it is a kind of drama.

clue.text: Way to pay party member wanting social skills

parts.note: a Con is a member of the Conservative Party
lacking diplomacy or social grace is being tactless

explanation.surface: A clumsy party member pays in some particular way, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is short for Conservative, a member of the UK party.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapping a card or phone on a reader is a payment method needing no physical swipe or PIN.

clue.text: Scholar to witter interminably

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter of the chatter word is dropped

parts.note: to witter is to chatter on, which in British slang is to rabbit

explanation.surface: A learned person is told to chatter on without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to RABBIT (on) is to talk at length; 'interminably' removes its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher learned in the law is a scholar of scripture.

clue.text: One deadly in play stopped getting put on pitch

parts.note: the venomous snake that kills Cleopatra in Shakespeare's play is an asp
stopped means halted

explanation.surface: A lethal player in a match halted, as if after being sent onto the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a sports field but is the tar-like surfacing material.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is a pitch-based surfacing, so a road coated with it has had pitch spread on it.

clue.text: New moves in confusing kind of war

indicators.note: the letter for new shifts its position further into the word for confusing

parts.note: something confusing is unclear

explanation.surface: Fresh tactics make a war harder to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves in' shifts the N of UNCLEAR one place inward, to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic war fought with fission or fusion weapons is the familiar label for that kind of conflict.

clue.text: Head off from state close to Connecticut

parts.note: to state is to aver, to assert

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A traveller turns away from a state near Connecticut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a US state beside Connecticut but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To head off trouble is to prevent or ward it off.

clue.text: Den broken into leaves damaged locks

indicators.note: into says the jumbled letters go inside the other word

parts.note: someone who leaves in a hurry splits, in slang

indicators.note: broken means the letters of 'Den' are smashed and reset

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks into a den, leaving the locks damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests a door but means hair; 'broken' shuffles Den, and 'into' places the result inside the slang word for leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair whose tips have frayed apart is damaged, and locks is a poetic word for hair.

clue.text: Career politician must do this to get elected

definitions.meaning: to career is to rush headlong, to speed along

definitions.text: politician must do this to get elected
definitions.meaning: a candidate must stand for office in an election

explanation.surface: A politician has to go for it to win office.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to dash, and one stands for office in an election campaign by the same verb.

clue.text: Cut bread the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means read backwards

parts.note: buns are small bread rolls

explanation.surface: Someone slices a loaf against the grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like slicing but means to ignore someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone dead is to ignore them deliberately, a social slight.

clue.text: Striking protest film's cut choice bit of dialogue

parts.note: a choice is a pick, as in the pick of the bunch

indicators.note: cut means the possessive ending is chopped off

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film, with its possessive S
an actor speaks a line of dialogue

explanation.surface: A striking scene in a protest film is a chosen piece of dialogue that got edited out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the S from ETS, leaving ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Strikers form a picket line outside a workplace as their form of protest.

clue.text: Repartee deficient amongst the elderly?

parts.note: deficient, poor in quality, means bad
amongst means in
the elderly are those in age, old age

explanation.surface: Banter is in short supply among old people, or so it is suggested.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light witty banter, the same as quick-fire repartee.

clue.text: A tiny bit dry wearing hat

indicators.note: wearing means the second piece is inside the hat word, the hat on top

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, dry

explanation.surface: A teetotaller wears only the smallest scrap of a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE is dated British slang for a hat; TT means teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tittle is the smallest particle or jot, as in 'not one jot or tittle'.

clue.text: Have kittens or seals gone swimming?

indicators.note: swimming means the letters of 'or seals gone' float about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone panics on seeing that the seals have swum away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have kittens' looks like breeding cats but is British slang for getting very upset; LOSE ONE'S RAG means lose one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are British idioms for becoming highly agitated or flying into a rage.

clue.text: Concerned with building support walls about river

indicators.note: walls is a verb here: the support piece encloses the next

parts.note: a strut is a brace that supports
C is short for circa, about
the Ural is a river in Russia

explanation.surface: A building's support walls run round a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walls' is a verb, enclosing C (circa) in the support word; the Ural is a Russian river.
explanation.definitionFit: Structural describes anything relating to the framework or construction of a building.

clue.text: Sap departs dressed in a continental fur

indicators.note: dressed in means the departure letter is wrapped inside the clothing words

parts.note: un is French for a
ermine is a white winter fur
D stands for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: A fool leaves wearing a European fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sap' looks like a fool but is a verb meaning to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap someone's strength is to wear it away gradually, as tunnelling weakens a wall.

clue.text: She'll clean hem of Lycra strip

indicators.note: a hem is a garment's edge, so the first and last letters of the word are taken

parts.note: to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A woman will tidy the hem of a Lycra outfit before taking it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose job is washing and ironing clothes cleans them for a living.

clue.text: Youngster repelled by hotel food

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so read backwards

parts.note: a youngster is a son
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A child is put off by the meals at a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food or a meal.

clue.text: Tried to abandon a group of animals

indicators.note: the word for tried leaves out the letter A

parts.note: a court that tried a case heard it

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to desert a group of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group of cattle or similar animals kept or living together.

clue.text: Projectile with function to retain oxygen when hot air's emitted?

parts.note: a discus is thrown in athletics

indicators.note: to retain means hold inside, so the gas symbol goes within

parts.note: sin is short for sine, a trigonometric function
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A thrown object works by trapping air when heated, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot air' looks scientific but means empty talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is an occasion of much talk, and hot air is a jokey phrase for idle verbiage.

clue.text: Legal order's problems fixing day

indicators.note: fixing means fastening the day inside the problems

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems
Mon is short for Monday

explanation.surface: A court's order deals with issues by setting a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A summons is a court order requiring someone to appear.

clue.text: Old city stores certainly a source of interest

indicators.note: stores means holds inside, the city word enclosing the next

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: Shops in an ancient city are definitely intriguing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' looks like curiosity but is money charged on a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging exorbitant rates is a source of interest on loans.

clue.text: Radius, not quite so long, is set?

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: so long, goodbye, is adios in Spanish

explanation.surface: A query whether a radius, made a bit shorter, is fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a noun: a receiver.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio is a receiving apparatus, and a wireless set is the old term for one.

clue.text: Damned irritated and extremely exasperated?

indicators.note: irritated letters are stirred up, so 'Damned' is rearranged
extremely means take the extreme letters, first and last

explanation.surface: Someone is very irritated and thoroughly exasperated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritated' rearranges DAMNED into MADDEN; 'extremely' takes E and D from exasperated. The whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being driven to fury or great annoyance is the meaning, as with someone damned irritated.

clue.text: Not all there, when voicing final words

indicators.note: Not all there says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone a bit dotty speaks their last words.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is a short closing stanza of a poem, a concluding statement.

clue.text: Maybe Hannah's daughter welcomed by Italian friend?

indicators.note: welcomed by means the letter is taken in by the following words

parts.note: a friend in Italy is a pal in Rome

explanation.surface: Perhaps Hannah's daughter is received by an Italian friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hannah's' means Hannah is: the name reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A word reading the same backwards and forwards is the category Hannah is an example of.

clue.text: Strip lights to give some electricity

indicators.note: strip means remove the outer layer, so both ends go

parts.note: lamps are lights

explanation.surface: Fluorescent strip lights supply a little power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip lights' looks like a tube fitting but 'Strip' trims LAMPS at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampere is the unit of current, so a measure of electrical flow.

clue.text: Switch egg supplier short of an egg

indicators.note: short of means lacking the letter that follows

parts.note: the ovary produces eggs
O looks like an egg

explanation.surface: Change the egg supplier, who is one egg short.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch something is to alter or change it.

clue.text: Fetching piano that needs taking back

parts.note: P is the musical notation for piano, softly
reclaiming goods on unpaid debt is repossessing

explanation.surface: Collecting a piano that has to be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' looks like collecting but means attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching and this word both describe a person who is attractive and pleasing to look at.
